claim: F_q[T], exact integers, q = 7 (columns up to degree 14) and q = 13 (up to 12), pre-registered. Completed marked rows in the window N - lam < d < N + lam with dual length above 3N: energy/diagonal of the probe vector of a Weil target grows with the active dual length (q = 7: 1.2 to 20.6 over 9 sizes, slope of log_q excess +0.30; q = 13: 2.2 to 18.1, slope +0.25); trivial-target vector +0.60 (3 sizes). Rule outcome: the window statement FAILS in the model, as predicted. Controls: Liouville-twisted vector up to 951 and 2452 times the diagonal; aligned vector at the operator-norm size; random phases at the diagonal in 30 of 30. Completed rows are polynomial coefficients (exact, 5 cases). N = 3: the cube term Jbar V S_0 with trivial cofactor carries the energy (6.3 against 0.8; 40 against 0.6) and lifts target vectors above the diagonal at dual length at or below 3N (2.4 to 5.5, both q); pivot rule UNDECIDED. Reflected dual sums NOT-RUN.
errors: No referee pass. 22 of 109 advance interval predictions missed (12 for the trivial-target vector, where the round-8 law has the wrong inactive classes; 10 by factors up to 1.5 high or 3 low). The prediction that completion changes the energy by at most 30% missed where the cube term is active. Pivot rule came out UNDECIDED (criterion fails for the trivial-target vector). Five pre-registered sizes dropped for time. One validation unit killed by its memory limit inside the round-8 reference program (limit not raised, size reduced); one duplicate job started by my error and stopped.
surviving: Model statement only, no statement about zeta: in the window the row mean square of the probe vector is the diagonal plus squared signals of the vector's Moebius sums; beyond dual length 3N it exceeds the diagonal with a positive exponent for targets with square-root cancellation, at both q. For completed rows at N = 3 the cube part contributes a squared signal with trivial cofactor that exceeds the diagonal already at dual length at or below 3N.
lesson: A completed row T = L_0 D carries one squared signal per cube step, with cofactor length N - 3j; the shortest cofactor has the least Moebius cancellation and can dominate the energy. Test the completed object, not its squarefree part. A coherent law fitted on twisted targets can have the wrong inactive classes for the trivial target.
followUp: Completed rows at N = 6 (j = 2), one run (6, 9, 2) at q = 7, to test the argued threshold r > 2N - 3 for completed rows; compare the cube term with the manuscript signal of section 7.2.
